claim: Single-cell RNA-Seq (scRNA-Seq) can quantify transcripts in individual cells.
source: Although single-cell RNA-Seq (scRNA-Seq) can quantify transcripts in individual cells, each cell's expression profile may be a mixture of both types of programs, making them difficult to disentangle.
evidence: This is established knowledge about scRNA-Seq technology capabilities.

claim: Each cell's expression profile may be a mixture of identity and activity programs, making them difficult to disentangle.
source: Although single-cell RNA-Seq (scRNA-Seq) can quantify transcripts in individual cells, each cell's expression profile may be a mixture of both types of programs, making them difficult to disentangle.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the nature of gene expression and the challenge addressed by the study.

claim: Consensus non-negative matrix factorization (cNMF) accurately infers identity and activity programs in simulations.
source: We show with simulations that a method we call consensus non-negative matrix factorization (cNMF) accurately infers identity and activity programs, including their relative contributions in each cell.
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: cNMF can infer the relative contributions of identity and activity programs in each cell.
source: We show with simulations that a method we call consensus non-negative matrix factorization (cNMF) accurately infers identity and activity programs, including their relative contributions in each cell.
evidence: This is demonstrated through simulation results shown in the manuscript.

claim: cNMF refines cell types in brain organoid scRNA-Seq datasets.
source: To illustrate the insights this approach enables, we apply it to published brain organoid and visual cortex scRNA-Seq datasets; cNMF refines cell types and identifies both expected (e.g. cell cycle and hypoxia) and novel activity programs, including programs that may underlie a neurosecretory phenotype and synaptogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by the analysis of the Quadrato et al. (2017) brain organoid dataset.

claim: cNMF identifies cell cycle activity programs in brain organoid data.
source: To illustrate the insights this approach enables, we apply it to published brain organoid and visual cortex scRNA-Seq datasets; cNMF refines cell types and identifies both expected (e.g. cell cycle and hypoxia) and novel activity programs, including programs that may underlie a neurosecretory phenotype and synaptogenesis.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the brain organoid dataset.

claim: cNMF identifies hypoxia activity programs in brain organoid data.
source: To illustrate the insights this approach enables, we apply it to published brain organoid and visual cortex scRNA-Seq datasets; cNMF refines cell types and identifies both expected (e.g. cell cycle and hypoxia) and novel activity programs, including programs that may underlie a neurosecretory phenotype and synaptogenesis.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the brain organoid dataset.

claim: cNMF identifies novel activity programs that may underlie a neurosecretory phenotype.
source: To illustrate the insights this approach enables, we apply it to published brain organoid and visual cortex scRNA-Seq datasets; cNMF refines cell types and identifies both expected (e.g. cell cycle and hypoxia) and novel activity programs, including programs that may underlie a neurosecretory phenotype and synaptogenesis.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the genes identified in the novel activity program.

claim: cNMF identifies novel activity programs that may underlie synaptogenesis.
source: To illustrate the insights this approach enables, we apply it to published brain organoid and visual cortex scRNA-Seq datasets; cNMF refines cell types and identifies both expected (e.g. cell cycle and hypoxia) and novel activity programs, including programs that may underlie a neurosecretory phenotype and synaptogenesis.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the genes identified in the novel activity program.

claim: Genes act in concert to maintain a cell's identity as a specific cell type.
source: Genes act in concert to maintain a cell's identity as a specific cell type, to respond to external signals, and to carry out complex cellular activities such as replication and metabolism.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about gene function.

claim: Coordinating genes for cellular functions is frequently achieved through transcriptional co-regulation.
source: Coordinating the necessary genes for these functions is frequently achieved through transcriptional co-regulation, where genes are induced together as a gene expression program (GEP) in response to the appropriate internal or external signal (Eisen et al., 1998; Segal et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: RNA-Seq enables unbiased measurement of the whole transcriptome.
source: By enabling unbiased measurement of the whole transcriptome, profiling technologies such as RNA-Seq are paving the way for systematically discovering GEPs and shedding light on the biological mechanisms that they govern (Liberzon et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about RNA-Seq technology, supported by citation.

claim: Single-cell RNA-Seq has greatly enhanced the potential to resolve gene expression programs by making it possible to observe variation in gene expression over many individual cells.
source: Single-cell RNA-Seq (scRNA-Seq) has greatly enhanced our potential to resolve GEPs by making it possible to observe variation in gene expression over many individual cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the advantages of scRNA-Seq technology.

claim: Inferring gene expression programs from scRNA-Seq data remains challenging because the data is noisy and high-dimensional.
source: Even so, inferring GEPs remains challenging as scRNA-Seq data is noisy and high-dimensional, requiring computational approaches to uncover the underlying patterns.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the challenges of scRNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: Technical artifacts such as doublets can confound scRNA-Seq analysis.
source: In addition, technical artifacts such as doublets (where two or more distinct cells are mistakenly collapsed into one) can confound analysis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about technical challenges in scRNA-Seq.

claim: Individual cells may express multiple gene expression programs but we only detect cellular expression profiles that reflect their combination.
source: Here, we focus on a key challenge of inferring expression programs from scRNA-Seq data: the fact that individual cells may express multiple GEPs but we only detect cellular expression profiles that reflect their combination, rather than the GEPs themselves.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the nature of gene expression measurement in single cells.

claim: A cell's gene expression is shaped by its cell type, its state in time-dependent processes such as the cell cycle, and its response to varied environmental stimuli.
source: A cell's gene expression is shaped by many factors including its cell type, its state in time-dependent processes such as the cell cycle, and its response to varied environmental stimuli (Wagner et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Identity programs are expressed uniquely in cells of a specific cell type.
source: In this formulation, identity programs are expressed uniquely in cells of a specific cell type, while activity programs may vary dynamically in cells of one or multiple types and may be continuous or discrete.
evidence: This is a definition provided by the authors for their framework.

claim: Activity programs may vary dynamically in cells of one or multiple types and may be continuous or discrete.
source: In this formulation, identity programs are expressed uniquely in cells of a specific cell type, while activity programs may vary dynamically in cells of one or multiple types and may be continuous or discrete.
evidence: This is a definition provided by the authors for their framework.

claim: The vast majority of scRNA-Seq studies have focused on systematically identifying and characterizing the expression programs of cell types composing a given tissue.
source: Thus far, the vast majority of scRNA-Seq studies have focused on systematically identifying and characterizing the expression programs of cell types composing a given tissue, that is identity GEPs.
evidence: This is an observation about the state of the field based on the authors' knowledge.

claim: Substantially less progress has been made in identifying activity gene expression programs.
source: Substantially less progress has been made in identifying activity GEPs, primarily through direct manipulation of cells in controlled experiments, for example comparing stimulated and unstimulated neurons (Hrvatin et al., 2018) or cells pre- and post-viral infection (Steuerman et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an observation about the state of the field supported by citations.

claim: Finding the average expression of clusters of similar cells may often be sufficient for finding reasonably accurate identity gene expression programs.
source: Thus, while finding the average expression of clusters of similar cells may often be sufficient for finding reasonably accurate identity GEPs, it will often fail for activity GEPs.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of clustering approaches.

claim: Finding the average expression of clusters of similar cells will often fail for activity gene expression programs.
source: Thus, while finding the average expression of clusters of similar cells may often be sufficient for finding reasonably accurate identity GEPs, it will often fail for activity GEPs.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of clustering approaches.

claim: Matrix factorization can model the gene expression data matrix as the product of two lower rank matrices.
source: In this context, matrix factorization would model the gene expression data matrix as the product of two lower rank matrices, one encoding the relative contribution of each gene to each program, and a second specifying the proportions in which the programs are combined for each cell.
evidence: This is established knowledge about matrix factorization methods.

claim: Matrix factorization allows cells to express multiple gene expression programs.
source: Unlike hard clustering, which reduces all cells in a cluster to a single shared GEP, matrix factorization allows cells to express multiple GEPs.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the properties of matrix factorization compared to clustering.

claim: Matrix factorization could correctly model doublets as a combination of the identity gene expression programs for the combined cell types.
source: Thus, this computational approach would allow cells to express one or more activity GEPs in addition to their expected cell-type GEP, and could correctly model doublets as a combination of the identity GEPs for the combined cell types.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the potential of matrix factorization to handle doublets.

claim: No previously reported studies have benchmarked the ability of matrix factorization methods to accurately learn identity and activity gene expression programs from scRNA-Seq profiles.
source: To the best of our knowledge, no previously reported studies have benchmarked the ability of matrix factorization methods to accurately learn identity and activity GEPs from scRNA-Seq profiles.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the work based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: Systematic discovery of gene expression programs could reveal unexpected or novel activity programs reflecting important biological processes in the context of the native biological tissue.
source: First, systematic discovery of GEPs could reveal unexpected or novel activity programs reflecting important biological processes (e.g. immune activation or hypoxia) in the context of the native biological tissue.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the potential benefits of the approach.

claim: Inferring gene expression programs could enable characterization of the prevalence of each activity program across cell types in the tissue.
source: Second, it could enable characterization of the prevalence of each activity GEP across cell types in the tissue.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the potential benefits of the approach.

claim: Accounting for activity programs could improve inference of identity programs by avoiding spurious inclusion of activity program genes in the latter.
source: Finally, accounting for activity programs could improve inference of identity programs by avoiding spurious inclusion of activity program genes in the latter.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the benefits of jointly modeling identity and activity programs.

claim: Gene expression programs corresponding to different phases of the cell cycle are examples of widespread activity programs.
source: GEPs corresponding to different phases of the cell cycle are examples of widespread activity programs and are well-known to confound identity (cell type) program inference in scRNA-Seq data (Chen and Zhou, 2017; Scialdone et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Cell-cycle gene expression programs are well-known to confound identity (cell type) program inference in scRNA-Seq data.
source: GEPs corresponding to different phases of the cell cycle are examples of widespread activity programs and are well-known to confound identity (cell type) program inference in scRNA-Seq data (Chen and Zhou, 2017; Scialdone et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) has been used for dimensionality reduction of scRNA-Seq data prior to downstream analysis.
source: In particular, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Independent Component Analysis (ICA), Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) (Blei et al., 2003) and Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF)(Lee and Seung, 1999) have been used for dimensionality reduction of data prior to downstream analysis or as an approach to cell clustering.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the use of PCA in scRNA-Seq analysis.

claim: PCA components have been interpreted as activity programs.
source: However, while PCA (Shalek et al., 2014; Steuerman et al., 2018), NMF (Puram et al., 2017) and ICA (Saunders et al., 2018) components have been interpreted as activity programs, the dimensions inferred by these or other matrix factorization algorithms may not necessarily align with biologically meaningful gene expression programs and are frequently ignored in practice.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: NMF components have been interpreted as activity programs.
source: However, while PCA (Shalek et al., 2014; Steuerman et al., 2018), NMF (Puram et al., 2017) and ICA (Saunders et al., 2018) components have been interpreted as activity programs, the dimensions inferred by these or other matrix factorization algorithms may not necessarily align with biologically meaningful gene expression programs and are frequently ignored in practice.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ICA components have been interpreted as activity programs.
source: However, while PCA (Shalek et al., 2014; Steuerman et al., 2018), NMF (Puram et al., 2017) and ICA (Saunders et al., 2018) components have been interpreted as activity programs, the dimensions inferred by these or other matrix factorization algorithms may not necessarily align with biologically meaningful gene expression programs and are frequently ignored in practice.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The dimensions inferred by matrix factorization algorithms may not necessarily align with biologically meaningful gene expression programs.
source: However, while PCA (Shalek et al., 2014; Steuerman et al., 2018), NMF (Puram et al., 2017) and ICA (Saunders et al., 2018) components have been interpreted as activity programs, the dimensions inferred by these or other matrix factorization algorithms may not necessarily align with biologically meaningful gene expression programs and are frequently ignored in practice.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of matrix factorization methods.

claim: NMF and LDA are non-negative and so cannot directly model repression.
source: For example, NMF and LDA are non-negative and so cannot directly model repression.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the mathematical properties of NMF and LDA.

claim: ICA components are statistically independent.
source: ICA components are statistically independent, PCA components are mutually orthogonal, and both allow gene expression to be negative.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the properties of ICA.

claim: PCA components are mutually orthogonal.
source: ICA components are statistically independent, PCA components are mutually orthogonal, and both allow gene expression to be negative.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the properties of PCA.

claim: ICA and PCA both allow gene expression to be negative.
source: ICA components are statistically independent, PCA components are mutually orthogonal, and both allow gene expression to be negative.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the properties of ICA and PCA.

claim: LDA explicitly accounts for the count distribution of expression data in its error model.
source: Furthermore, none of these methods, except LDA, explicitly accounts for the count distribution of expression data in their error models.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the properties of LDA.

claim: ICA, LDA, and NMF—but not PCA—can accurately discover both activity and identity gene expression programs despite their simplifying assumptions.
source: Using simulations, we show that despite their simplifying assumptions, ICA, LDA, and NMF—but not PCA—can accurately discover both activity and identity GEPs.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: ICA, LDA, and NMF give substantially varying results when repeated multiple times due to inherent randomness in their algorithms.
source: However, due to inherent randomness in their algorithms, they give substantially varying results when repeated multiple times, which hinders their interpretability.
evidence: This is demonstrated through simulation results shown in the manuscript.

claim: A meta-analysis approach demonstrably increased robustness and accuracy of matrix factorization methods.
source: We therefore implemented a meta-analysis approach (Figure 1B), which demonstrably increased robustness and accuracy.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Consensus NMF (cNMF) gave the best performance in simulations.
source: Overall, the meta-analysis of NMF, which we call Consensus NMF (cNMF), gave the best performance in these simulations.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: cNMF inferred expected activity programs (cell-cycle programs) in a brain organoid dataset.
source: Applied to three real datasets generated by three different scRNA-Seq platforms, cNMF inferred expected activity programs (cell-cycle programs in a brain organoid dataset and depolarization induced programs in visual cortex neurons), an unanticipated hypoxia program, and intriguing novel activity programs.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the brain organoid dataset.

claim: cNMF inferred expected activity programs (depolarization induced programs) in visual cortex neurons.
source: Applied to three real datasets generated by three different scRNA-Seq platforms, cNMF inferred expected activity programs (cell-cycle programs in a brain organoid dataset and depolarization induced programs in visual cortex neurons), an unanticipated hypoxia program, and intriguing novel activity programs.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the visual cortex dataset.

claim: cNMF inferred an unanticipated hypoxia program in brain organoid data.
source: Applied to three real datasets generated by three different scRNA-Seq platforms, cNMF inferred expected activity programs (cell-cycle programs in a brain organoid dataset and depolarization induced programs in visual cortex neurons), an unanticipated hypoxia program, and intriguing novel activity programs.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of the brain organoid dataset.

claim: cNMF enhanced cell type characterization in real datasets.
source: It also enhanced cell type characterization and enabled estimation of rates of activity across cell types.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of real datasets.

claim: cNMF enabled estimation of rates of activity across cell types in real datasets.
source: It also enhanced cell type characterization and enabled estimation of rates of activity across cell types.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of real datasets.

claim: The simulated data consisted of 15,000 cells composed of 13 cell types, one cellular activity program, and a 6% doublet rate.
source: We evaluated this in simulated data of 15,000 cells composed of 13 cell types, one cellular activity program that is active to varying extents in a subset of cells of four cell types, and a 6% doublet rate (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the parameters of the simulation used in the study.

claim: The activity program in the simulation is active to varying extents in a subset of cells of four cell types.
source: We evaluated this in simulated data of 15,000 cells composed of 13 cell types, one cellular activity program that is active to varying extents in a subset of cells of four cell types, and a 6% doublet rate (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the parameters of the simulation used in the study.

claim: cNMF was most accurate at inferring genes in the activity program, with a sensitivity of 61% at a false discovery rate (FDR) of 5%.
source: We found that cNMF was most accurate at inferring genes in the activity program, with a sensitivity of 61% at a false discovery rate (FDR) of 5% (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: cICA and the ground-truth clustering were the next most accurate at inferring genes in the activity program with 57% and 56% sensitivity at a 5% FDR, respectively.
source: cICA and the ground-truth clustering were the next most accurate with 57% and 56% sensitivity at a 5% FDR, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: cNMF performed the best at inferring identity gene expression programs of the 4 cell types that expressed the activity program.
source: cNMF also performed the best at inferring identity GEPs of the 4 cell types that expressed the activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: Clustering approaches performed worse at inferring identity gene expression programs because they inappropriately assigned activity program genes to these identity programs, resulting in an elevated FDR.
source: As expected, the clustering approaches performed worse as they inappropriately assigned activity GEP genes to these identity programs, resulting in an elevated FDR.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the simulation results.

claim: cNMF yielded the most accurate inferences in simulated data.
source: We decided to proceed with cNMF to analyze the real datasets due its accuracy, processing speed, and interpretability. First, it yielded the most accurate inferences in our simulated data.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NMF was the fastest of the basic factorization algorithms considered.
source: Second, NMF was the fastest of the basic factorization algorithms considered, which is especially useful given the need to run multiple replicates and given the growing sizes of scRNA-Seq datasets (Figure 2—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is supported by runtime comparison data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6.

claim: The non-negativity assumption of NMF naturally results in usage and component matrices that can be normalized and interpreted as probability distributions.
source: Third, the non-negativity assumption of NMF naturally results in usage and component matrices that can be normalized and interpreted as probability distributions—that is, where the usage matrix reflects the probability of each GEP being used in each cell, and the component matrix reflects the probability of a specific transcript expressed in a GEP being a specific gene.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the mathematical properties of NMF.

claim: cNMF could accurately infer which cells expressed the activity program and what proportion of their expression was derived from the activity program.
source: Beyond identifying the activity program itself, we found that cNMF could also accurately infer which cells expressed the activity program and what proportion of their expression was derived from the activity program (Figure 2f).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2f.

claim: With an expression usage threshold of 10%, cNMF accurately classified 91% of cells expressing the activity program and 94% of cells that did not express the program.
source: With an expression usage threshold of 10%, cNMF accurately classified 91% of cells expressing the activity program and 94% of cells that did not express the program.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: There was a high Pearson correlation (R = 0.74 for all simulations combined, R = 0.68 for the example simulation) between the inferred and simulated usages in cells that expressed the activity program.
source: Moreover, we observed a high Pearson correlation between the inferred and simulated usages in cells that expressed the program (R = 0.74 for all simulations combined, R = 0.68 for the example simulation in Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: cNMF correctly modeled doublets as a combination of the gene expression programs for the two combined cell types.
source: We found that cNMF correctly modeled doublets as a combination of the GEPs for the two combined cell types (Figure 2g).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2g.

claim: cNMF could accurately infer the gene expression programs even in a simulated dataset composed of 50% doublets.
source: Moreover, we found that cNMF could accurately infer the GEPs even in a simulated dataset composed of 50% doublets (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: cNMF identified 31 distinct programs in the brain organoid dataset that could be further parsed into identity and activity programs.
source: We identified 31 distinct programs in this dataset that could be further parsed into identity and activity programs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the brain organoid dataset shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Most cells in the brain organoid dataset had high usage of just a single gene expression program.
source: Most cells had high usage of just a single GEP, which is consistent with expressing just an identity program (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the brain organoid dataset shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Three gene expression programs in the brain organoid dataset were co-expressed with many distinct and uncorrelated programs, suggesting that they represent activity programs that occur across diverse cell types.
source: By contrast, three GEPs were co-expressed with many distinct and uncorrelated programs, suggesting that they represent activity programs that occur across diverse cell types (Figure 3a–b).
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-expression patterns observed in the data.

claim: The 28 suspected identity programs in the brain organoid dataset were well separated by the cell-type clusters reported in Quadrato et al. (2017).
source: Consistent with this, the 28 suspected identity programs were well separated by the cell-type clusters reported in Quadrato et al. (2017) while the three suspected activity programs were expressed by cells across multiple clusters (Figure 3—figure supplements 3–4).
evidence: This is supported by analysis comparing cNMF results to published clusters.

claim: The three suspected activity programs in the brain organoid dataset were expressed by cells across multiple clusters.
source: Consistent with this, the 28 suspected identity programs were well separated by the cell-type clusters reported in Quadrato et al. (2017) while the three suspected activity programs were expressed by cells across multiple clusters (Figure 3—figure supplements 3–4).
evidence: This is supported by analysis comparing cNMF results to published clusters.

claim: Cells previously annotated as mesodermal in the brain organoid dataset predominantly expressed one of three gene expression programs that were significantly enriched for genes in the 'Muscle Contraction' Gene Ontology set.
source: For example, we noticed that cells previously annotated as mesodermal predominantly expressed one of three GEPs that were significantly enriched for genes in the 'Muscle Contraction' Gene Ontology (GO) set (p<1×10−10 vs. p>0.19 for all other GEPs).
evidence: This is supported by gene set enrichment analysis of the brain organoid data.

claim: Three gene expression programs in the brain organoid dataset likely represent muscle cells.
source: For example, we noticed that cells previously annotated as mesodermal predominantly expressed one of three GEPs that were significantly enriched for genes in the 'Muscle Contraction' Gene Ontology (GO) set (p<1×10−10 vs. p>0.19 for all other GEPs). They therefore likely represent muscle cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on gene set enrichment analysis.

claim: Three gene expression programs in the brain organoid dataset include genes characteristic of different classes of skeletal muscle: immature skeletal muscle, fast-twitch muscle, and slow-twitch muscle.
source: Inspecting the genes associated with these three GEPs, we noticed that they include genes characteristic of different classes of skeletal muscle: (1) immature skeletal muscle (e.g. MYOG, TNNT2, NES), (2) fast-twitch muscle (e.g. TNNT3, TNNC2, MYOZ1), and (3) slow-twitch muscle (e.g. TNNT1, TNNC1, TPM3) (Figure 3d, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by inspection of genes in the programs shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Distinct populations of skeletal muscle cells are differentiating in brain organoids.
source: This unexpected finding suggests that distinct populations of skeletal muscle cells -- excitatory cell types with many similarities to neurons -- are differentiating in these brain organoids.
evidence: This is an inference based on the identification of muscle-related gene expression programs.

claim: Two activity programs in the brain organoid dataset were strongly enriched for cell cycle Gene Ontology sets, suggesting that they correspond to separate phases of the cell cycle.
source: Of the three activity programs identified, we found that two were strongly enriched for cell cycle Gene Ontology (GO) sets, suggesting that they correspond to separate phases of the cell cycle (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is supported by gene set enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3c.

claim: One cell cycle activity program in the brain organoid dataset represents a G1/S checkpoint program.
source: These enrichments and inspection of the genes most associated with these programs implied that one represents a G1/S checkpoint program and the other represents a G2/M checkpoint program (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is an inference based on gene set enrichment and gene inspection shown in Figure 3e.

claim: One cell cycle activity program in the brain organoid dataset represents a G2/M checkpoint program.
source: These enrichments and inspection of the genes most associated with these programs implied that one represents a G1/S checkpoint program and the other represents a G2/M checkpoint program (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is an inference based on gene set enrichment and gene inspection shown in Figure 3e.

claim: The third activity program in the brain organoid dataset is characterized by high levels of hypoxia related genes, suggesting it represents a hypoxia program.
source: The third activity program is characterized by high levels of hypoxia related genes (e.g. VEGFA, PGK1, CA9, P4HA1, HILPDA) suggesting it represents a hypoxia program (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is an inference based on the genes identified in the program shown in Figure 3e.

claim: The lack of vasculature in organoids makes hypoxia an important growth constraint.
source: This is consistent with the lack of vasculature in organoids which makes hypoxia an important growth constraint (Kelava and Lancaster, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The hypoxia gene expression program in the brain organoid dataset is most significantly enriched for genesets related to protein localization to the endoplasmic reticulum and nonsense mediated decay.
source: This GEP is most significantly enriched for genesets related to protein localization to the endoplasmic reticulum and nonsense mediated decay (p=3×10−37, p=5×10−31) (Figure 3c), consistent with reports that hypoxia post-transcriptionally increases expression of genes that are translated in the ER (Staudacher et al., 2015) and modulates nonsense mediated decay activity (Gardner, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by gene set enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3c and citations to prior work.

claim: Hypoxia post-transcriptionally increases expression of genes that are translated in the ER.
source: This GEP is most significantly enriched for genesets related to protein localization to the endoplasmic reticulum and nonsense mediated decay (p=3×10−37, p=5×10−31) (Figure 3c), consistent with reports that hypoxia post-transcriptionally increases expression of genes that are translated in the ER (Staudacher et al., 2015) and modulates nonsense mediated decay activity (Gardner, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Hypoxia modulates nonsense mediated decay activity.
source: This GEP is most significantly enriched for genesets related to protein localization to the endoplasmic reticulum and nonsense mediated decay (p=3×10−37, p=5×10−31) (Figure 3c), consistent with reports that hypoxia post-transcriptionally increases expression of genes that are translated in the ER (Staudacher et al., 2015) and modulates nonsense mediated decay activity (Gardner, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: In the initial report of the brain organoid data, staining for HIF1A failed to detect significant levels of hypoxia.
source: In the initial report of this data, staining for a single hypoxia gene, HIF1A, failed to detect significant levels of hypoxia.
evidence: This is a reference to findings from the original publication of the dataset.

claim: HIF1A is not strongly associated with the hypoxia gene expression program in the brain organoid dataset, at least not at the transcriptional level.
source: Indeed, HIF1A is not strongly associated with this GEP, at least not at the transcriptional level.
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of the brain organoid data.

claim: 3079 cells (5.9%) in the brain organoid dataset expressed the G1/S program with usage >= 10%.
source: We found that 3079 cells (5.9%) expressed the G1/S program and 2043 cells (3.9%) expressed the G2/M program (with usage >= 10%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of the brain organoid data.

claim: 2043 cells (3.9%) in the brain organoid dataset expressed the G2/M program with usage >= 10%.
source: We found that 3079 cells (5.9%) expressed the G1/S program and 2043 cells (3.9%) expressed the G2/M program (with usage >= 10%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of the brain organoid data.

claim: cNMF detected a rare 'stem-like' population in the brain organoid dataset based on high expression of pluripotency markers.
source: For example, cNMF detected a rare population, included with the forebrain cluster in the original report, that we label as 'stem-like' based on high expression of pluripotency markers (e.g. LIN28A, L1TD1, MIR302B, DNMT3B) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the genes identified in the program.

claim: The 'stem-like' population in the brain organoid dataset showed the highest rates of proliferation with over 38% of cells expressing a cell-cycle program.
source: These cells showed the highest rates of proliferation with over 38% of them expressing a cell-cycle program in addition to the 'stem-like' identity GEP (Figure 3f).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis shown in Figure 3f.

claim: A cell cluster labeled in Quadrato et al. (2017) as 'proliferative precursors' is composed of multiple cell types including immature muscle and dopaminergic neurons.
source: For example, we found that a cell cluster labeled in Quadrato et al. (2017) as 'proliferative precursors', based on high expression of cell-cycle genes, is composed of multiple cell types including immature muscle and dopaminergic neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is an inference based on cNMF analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The predominant identity gene expression program of cells in the 'proliferative precursors' cluster is most strongly associated with the gene PAX7, a marker of self-renewing muscle stem cells.
source: The predominant identity GEP of cells in this cluster is most strongly associated with the gene PAX7, a marker of self-renewing muscle stem cells (Pawlikowski et al., 2009) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the genes in the program and citation to prior work.

claim: The hypoxia response program is widespread in the brain organoid dataset with 5788 cells (11%) of all cells expressing it (usage >10%).
source: The hypoxia response program is widespread in this dataset with 5788 cells (11%) of all cells expressing it (usage >10%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of the brain organoid data.

claim: cNMF identified 20 gene expression programs in the visual cortex dataset, interpreting 14 as identity and six as activity programs.
source: We ran cNMF on neurons combined from all three exposure conditions and identified 20 GEPs, interpreting 14 as identity and six as activity programs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of the visual cortex dataset shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the visual cortex dataset, the activity programs were co-expressed with many distinct and uncorrelated gene expression programs while the identity programs only overlapped in related cell types.
source: As we saw in the organoid data, the activity programs were co-expressed with many distinct and uncorrelated GEPs while the identity programs only overlapped in related cell types (Figure 4a–b).
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis shown in Figure 4a–b.

claim: In the visual cortex dataset, the identity programs were well separated by the published clusters while the activity programs were spread across multiple clusters.
source: In addition, the identity programs were well separated by the published clusters while the activity programs were spread across multiple clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by analysis comparing cNMF results to published clusters shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Three activity programs in the visual cortex dataset were correlated with the stimulus, indicating that they are induced by repeated depolarization.
source: Three activity programs were correlated with the stimulus, which indicates that they are induced by repeated depolarization (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation with experimental conditions shown in Figure 4c.

claim: One depolarization-induced activity program in the visual cortex dataset was induced at 1h and corresponds to an early response program (ERP).
source: One of these was induced at 1h and thus corresponds to an early response program (ERP).
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of induction.

claim: Two depolarization-induced activity programs in the visual cortex dataset were primarily induced at 4h and correspond to late response programs (LRPs).
source: The others were primarily induced at 4h and thus correspond to late response programs (LRPs).
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of induction.

claim: The depolarization-induced programs identified by cNMF overlapped significantly with the sets of differentially expressed genes reported in Hrvatin et al. (2018).
source: These programs overlapped significantly with the sets of differentially expressed genes reported in Hrvatin et al. (2018) (p=8×10−34 for the ERP and genes induced at 1h; p=4×10−22, p=4×10−14 for the LRPs and genes induced at 4hs, one-sided Mann Whitney test).
evidence: This is supported by statistical comparison with published results.

claim: One late response program in the visual cortex dataset was more induced in superficial cortical layers, while the other was more induced in deeper layers.
source: Intriguingly, one LRP was more induced in superficial cortical layers, while the other was more induced in deeper layers.
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of the visual cortex data.

claim: The early response program is predominantly shared across excitatory neurons, while late response programs vary more substantially across neuron subtypes.
source: This supports a recently proposed model where the ERP is predominantly shared across excitatory neurons, while LRPs vary more substantially across neuron subtypes (Hrvatin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference supported by the data and citation to prior work.

claim: In the initial report of the visual cortex data, only 64 and 53 genes were identified as differentially expressed in at least one excitatory cell type at 1h and 4hs (FC ≥2, FDR < 0.05).
source: It also illustrates cNMF's sensitivity: in the initial report, only 64 and 53 genes were identified as differentially expressed in at least one excitatory cell type at 1h and 4hs (FC ≥2, FDR < 0.05).
evidence: This is a reference to findings from the original publication of the dataset.

claim: cNMF was able to find the depolarization-induced program in an unsupervised manner, without knowledge of the experimental design.
source: Nevertheless, cNMF was able to find this program in an unsupervised manner, without knowledge of the experimental design.
evidence: This is a claim about the capabilities of cNMF demonstrated by the analysis.

claim: cNMF identified a gene expression program in the Tasic et al. (2016) visual cortex dataset that showed striking concordance with the superficial late response program found in the primary dataset (Fisher Exact Test OR = 127, p=1×10−118, Pearson Correlation = 0.645).
source: Moreover, it identified a GEP that showed striking concordance with the superficial LRP found in the primary dataset (Fisher Exact Test of genes with association z-score >0.0015, OR = 127, p=1×10−118, Pearson Correlation = 0.645) (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is supported by statistical comparison shown in Figure 4d.

claim: The superficial late response program in the Tasic et al. (2016) dataset was predominantly expressed in excitatory cells of the more superficial layers of the cortex.
source: This program was predominantly expressed in excitatory cells of the more superficial layers of the cortex as would be expected based on the results in the primary dataset.
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of the Tasic et al. (2016) dataset.

claim: Over 40% of the excitatory layer 2 (Exc. L2) type neurons in the Tasic et al. (2016) dataset expressed the superficial late response activity program.
source: For example, over 40% of the excitatory layer 2 (Exc. L2) type neurons expressed this activity program (Figure 4—figure supplement 3b).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3b.

claim: cNMF could find the depolarization induced activity program in scRNA-Seq of cells that had not been experimentally manipulated to elicit it.
source: This demonstrates that cNMF could also find the depolarization induced activity program in scRNA-Seq of cells that had not been experimentally manipulated to elicit it.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of the Tasic et al. (2016) dataset.

claim: cNMF identified three additional activity programs in the primary visual cortex dataset that were not well correlated with the light stimulus but were expressed broadly across multiple neuronal cell types.
source: Finally, cNMF identified three additional activity programs in the primary visual cortex dataset that were not well correlated with the light stimulus but were expressed broadly across multiple neuronal cell types (Figure 4b–c).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis shown in Figure 4b–c.

claim: The neurosecretory activity program in the visual cortex dataset is characterized by high expression of several secreted neuropeptides including Vgf, Adcyap1, Scg2, Cck, Scg3, and Dkk3.
source: We labeled one of these, that was specific to excitatory neurons, as Neurosecretory (NS) because it is characterized by high expression of several secreted neuropeptides including Vgf, Adcyap1, Scg2, Cck, Scg3, and Dkk3, and has high expression of genes that facilitate protein secretion such as Cpe, Cadps2, and Scamp5 (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of genes in the program.

claim: The neurosecretory activity program in the visual cortex dataset has high expression of genes that facilitate protein secretion such as Cpe, Cadps2, and Scamp5.
source: We labeled one of these, that was specific to excitatory neurons, as Neurosecretory (NS) because it is characterized by high expression of several secreted neuropeptides including Vgf, Adcyap1, Scg2, Cck, Scg3, and Dkk3, and has high expression of genes that facilitate protein secretion such as Cpe, Cadps2, and Scamp5 (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of genes in the program.

claim: VGF (VGF nerve growth factor inducible) is induced by nerve growth factor.
source: The top expressed gene—Vgf (VGF nerve growth factor inducible) is induced by nerve growth factor (Salton et al., 1991), suggesting that this program may be regulated by external growth factor signals.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The neurosecretory program may be regulated by external growth factor signals.
source: The top expressed gene—Vgf (VGF nerve growth factor inducible) is induced by nerve growth factor (Salton et al., 1991), suggesting that this program may be regulated by external growth factor signals.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the genes in the program.

claim: A matching neurosecretory program was found in the Tasic et al. (2016) dataset (Fisher Exact Test OR = 53.8, p=8×10−21, Pearson Correlation = 0.356).
source: Notably, we found a matching program in the Tasic Et, Al. dataset (Fisher Exact Test of genes with association z-score >0.0015, OR = 53.8, p=8×10−21, Pearson Correlation = 0.356) (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is supported by statistical comparison shown in Figure 4e.

claim: The neurosecretory activity program is reproducible across multiple single-cell datasets.
source: Thus, this neurosecretory activity program is reproducible across multiple single-cell datasets.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from finding the program in multiple datasets.

claim: The synaptogenesis activity program in the visual cortex dataset is characterized by expression of genes that play a crucial role in synapse formation, including Mef2c, Ncam1, Cadm1, Syt1, Syt4, Actb, Ywhaz, and Bicd1.
source: An additional activity program which we labeled Synaptogenesis (Syn) was characterized by expression of genes that play a crucial role in synapse formation, including the transcriptional regulator Mef2c (Barbosa et al., 2008; Flavell et al., 2008; Harrington et al., 2016), synaptic adhesion molecules Ncam1 (Hata et al., 2018) and Cadm1 (Biederer et al., 2002; Robbins et al., 2010), membrane vesicle traffickers Syt1 and Syt4, Actb which constitutes the predominant synapse cytoskeletal protein, and others with a strong connection to synapse biology such as Ywhaz (Foote et al., 2015; Ramser et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2015), Bicd1 (Aguirre-Chen et al., 2011; Li et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of genes in the program, supported by citations.

claim: The synaptogenesis activity program in the visual cortex dataset was significantly enriched for relevant Gene Ontology sets including postsynapse, glutamatergic synapse, postsynaptic density, and dendrite morphogenesis (p<=3.25×10−6).
source: It was also significantly enriched for relevant Gene Ontology sets including postsynapse, glutamatergic synapse, postsynaptic density, and dendrite morphogenesis (p<=3.25×10−6, Supplementary file 3) which further suggests its interpretation as a program involved in the formation or regulation of synapses.
evidence: This is supported by gene set enrichment analysis.

claim: The last activity program in the visual cortex dataset was characterized by high expression of the maternally expressed long non-coding RNA Meg3 and other genes associated with cerebral ischemic injury.
source: The last activity program (labeled Other) was characterized by high expression of the maternally expressed long non-coding RNA Meg3 (Yan et al., 2016) and other genes that are associated with cerebral ischemic injury (e.g. Glg1 [Zhang et al., 1996], Rtn1 [Gong et al., 2017]).
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of genes in the program, supported by citations.

claim: Matrix factorization represents cells as linear combinations of multiple gene expression programs.
source: In this study, we distinguished between cell type (identity) and cell type independent (activity) gene expression programs (GEPs) to motivate our use of matrix factorization, which represents cells as linear combinations of multiple GEPs.
evidence: This is a description of the mathematical approach used in the study.

claim: Some biological programs are not neatly classified as either identity or activity gene expression programs.
source: However, we note that some biological programs are not neatly classified as either identity or activity GEPs.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the limitations of the identity/activity distinction.

claim: Cell states reflecting oncogenic transformation blur the distinction between identity and activity gene expression programs.
source: For example, cell states reflecting oncogenic transformation, or a cell's position along a morphological gradient blur the distinction between identity and activity.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of the identity/activity framework.

claim: Stochastic fluctuations in individual transcription factors could result in coordinated gene expression changes.
source: In addition, stochastic fluctuations in individual transcription factors could result in coordinated gene expression changes (Thattai and van Oudenaarden, 2001) and might be better described as a third program category, rather than as an identity or activity GEP.
evidence: This is a logical inference supported by citation.

claim: Matrix factorization should, in principle, be appropriate for representing all gene expression states that can be reasonably approximated as a linear mixture of programs.
source: While the identity/activity distinction might not be appropriate in every case, matrix factorization should, in principle, be appropriate for representing all gene expression states that can be reasonably approximated as a linear mixture of programs.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the applicability of matrix factorization.

claim: ICA, LDA, and NMF can infer components that align well with gene expression programs despite their simplifying assumptions.
source: Furthermore, in this study, we have provided an empirical foundation for the use of matrix factorization to simultaneously infer identity and activity programs from scRNA-Seq data. We first show with simulations that despite their simplifying assumptions, ICA, LDA, and NMF (but not PCA) can infer components that align well with GEPs.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Due to the stochastic nature of ICA, LDA, and NMF algorithms, the interpretability and accuracy of individual solutions can be low.
source: However, due to the stochastic nature of these algorithms, the interpretability and accuracy of individual solutions can be low.
evidence: This is demonstrated through simulation results shown in the manuscript.

claim: A consensus approach empirically increased the accuracy and robustness of matrix factorization solutions.
source: This led us to develop a consensus approach that empirically increased the accuracy and robustness of the solutions.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: cNMF yielded results in interpretable units of gene expression (transcripts per million).
source: Moreover, it yielded results in interpretable units of gene expression (transcripts per million) and could accurately infer the percentage of each cell's expression that was derived from each GEP.
evidence: This is a description of the output of the cNMF method.

claim: cNMF could accurately infer the percentage of each cell's expression that was derived from each gene expression program.
source: Moreover, it yielded results in interpretable units of gene expression (transcripts per million) and could accurately infer the percentage of each cell's expression that was derived from each GEP.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: cNMF identified several unexpected but highly plausible programs, including a hypoxia program in brain organoids and a depolarization-induced activity program in untreated neurons.
source: We then explored the utility of cNMF on real data, recapitulating known GEPs, identifying novel ones, and further characterizing their usage. We first validated cNMF with several expected activity programs serving as positive controls. We then identified several unexpected but highly plausible programs, a hypoxia program in brain organoids and a depolarization-induced activity program in untreated neurons.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of real datasets.

claim: cNMF identified three novel programs in visual cortex neurons that may correspond to a neurosecratory phenotype, new synapse formation, and a stress response program.
source: Finally, we identified three novel programs in visual cortex neurons that we speculate may correspond to a neurosecratory phenotype, new synapse formation, and a stress response program.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the genes identified in the novel activity programs.

claim: cNMF clarified the underlying cell types in datasets by disentangling activity and identity programs from the mixed single-cell profiles.
source: Beyond simply discovering activity programs, cNMF clarified the underlying cell types in these datasets by disentangling activity and identity programs from the mixed single-cell profiles.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of real datasets.

claim: A brain organoid subpopulation initially annotated as proliferative precursors actually includes replicating cells of several cell types such as an immature skeletal muscle cell.
source: For example, we found that a brain organoid subpopulation that was initially annotated as proliferative precursors actually includes replicating cells of several cell types such as an immature skeletal muscle cell that is differentiating into slow-twitch and fast-twitch muscle populations.
evidence: This is an inference based on cNMF analysis of the brain organoid data.

claim: Joint analysis of identity and activity gene expression programs allowed quantification of the relative prevalence of activities across cell types.
source: Furthermore, joint analysis of identity and activity GEPs allowed us to quantify the relative prevalence of activities across cell types.
evidence: This is demonstrated through analysis of real datasets.

claim: In the visual cortex data, one depolarization-induced late response program was predominantly expressed in neurons of superficial cortical layers, while the other was mainly expressed in deeper layers.
source: For example, we found in the visual cortex data that one depolarization-induced late response program was predominantly expressed in neurons of superficial cortical layers, while the other was mainly expressed in deeper layers.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of the visual cortex data.

claim: An anatomical or developmental factor may underlie variability in the depolarization response in visual cortex neurons.
source: This suggests that an anatomical or developmental factor may underlie variability in the response.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed differences in program expression.

claim: Commonly used approaches based on clustering or pseudotemporal ordering of cells are poorly suited to achieve insights about activity programs from single-cell data.
source: While commonly used approaches based on clustering or pseudotemporal ordering of cells are poorly suited to achieve such insights from single-cell data, these findings emerge naturally from our matrix factorization approach.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of alternative approaches.

claim: All cNMF code is deposited on Github at https://github.com/dylkot/cNMF/.
source: We have made our tools and analyses easily accessible so that researchers can readily use cNMF and further develop on the approach. We have deposited all the cNMF code on Github https://github.com/dylkot/cNMF/ (Kotliar, 2019; copy archived at https://github.com/elifesciences-publications/cNMF) and have made available all of the analysis scripts for figures contained in this manuscript on Code Ocean (https://doi.org/10.24433/CO.9044782e-cb96-4733-8a4f-bf42c21399e6) for easy exploration and re-execution.
evidence: This is a statement about data and code availability.

source: We have made our tools and analyses easily accessible so that researchers can readily use cNMF and further develop on the approach. claim: The choice of the number of components (K) must ultimately reflect the resolution desired by the analyst.
source: While the choice of K must ultimately reflect the resolution desired by the analyst, we propose two simple decision aids based on (1) considering the trade-off between factorization stability and reconstruction error and (2) looking at the proportion of variance explained by K principal components to estimate the dimensionality of the data (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is guidance provided by the authors for using cNMF.

claim: Choosing consecutive values of K primarily influenced individual components at the margin, suggesting that cNMF may be robust to this choice within a reasonable range of options.
source: In addition, we noticed that choosing consecutive values of K primarily influenced individual components at the margin, suggesting that cNMF may be robust to this choice within a reasonable range of options (Figure 5 and 'Choosing the number of components' section of the Materials and methods).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 5.
